meta.title: The Ingest Pipeline
meta.subtitle: how an event gets accepted, enriched, filed and served
intro: This repository is one write path and one read path sharing a store. An event arrives at the gateway, is validated against a shared schema, and is [[appended to a durable log before the caller is acknowledged]]. Workers read log segments, enrich each record, and file it in the store. The API serves what has been filed.

The diagram is a line, not a loop: gateway → log → workers → store → API. Everything above that spine supports it — the shared schema, the auth gate, the metrics registry, the scheduler that compacts old generations. Everything to the right is what comes out.

Nearly every hard problem here turned out to be a [[durability]] problem rather than a throughput one — when to acknowledge, what to do with a poisoned segment, how to compact without losing a read. The tall structures are the parts that measure or gate.
meta.readIt: Hover any building for a plain description; the <mark>How it's built</mark> tab gives the implementation and the exact files behind it, and <mark>Condition</mark> lists what is currently wrong with it. Double-click a structure with <mark>↵ inside</mark> to see its parts.

groups.name: Node runtime
groups.note: One image, three commands (api, workers, scheduler) — anything inside this wall is an in-process call.

groups.name: Rust rewrite
groups.note: Compiles and passes tests, feature-gated behind MERIDIAN_RUST=1, which is set in no deployed environment.

nodes.name: Ingest gateway
nodes.does: The front door. Takes an HTTP POST, checks the envelope is well-formed and not stale, writes it to the durable log, and only then returns 202. If the log write fails the caller finds out.
nodes.built: A single handler mounted on the app. Validation is delegated, the log append is awaited before the response, and both outcomes bump a counter in the metrics registry.
nodes.condition: Rejects are counted but never sampled, so a schema change that starts failing 100% of traffic looks identical to normal rejection noise on the dashboard.

cites.note: envelope validation and the 24h staleness rule

nodes.name: Durable log
nodes.does: An append-only segment log. Every accepted event lands here first; this is the only thing standing between an acknowledged write and a lost one.
nodes.built: Newline-delimited JSON appended to a segment file, rolled at 64 MB. Segments are read back whole by id.
nodes.condition: Segment roll is not atomic and `head` lives in module state, so two processes writing the same segment will interleave lines.

nodes.name: Enrichment workers
nodes.does: Five shards chew through log segments, attach geo and org lookups to each record, and file the result. One fin per replica.
nodes.built: A shard filter over an FNV hash of the event id, driven by a timer per replica. Replica count comes from the deployment, not the code.
nodes.condition: No dead-letter path — a segment that throws stalls its shard permanently, and the cursor never advances past it.

cites.note: replica fan-out and the stalling cursor
replicas: 5 — the real source of the fin count

nodes.name: Record store
nodes.does: Four generations of the same data — current, daily, weekly, archive. Writes always land in current; reads walk the generations until they hit.
nodes.built: A generation list with put/get/compact. Reads fall through in order, so a cold record costs four lookups.

nodes.name: Public API
nodes.does: Serves filed records over HTTP. Everything external reads through here, behind the auth gate.
nodes.built: A server factory that installs the auth middleware, mounts ingest, and registers the read routes. Handlers are thin; serialisation is separate.
nodes.condition: The list route does an unbounded scan with no pagination — it is the endpoint every complaint is actually about.

children.name: Route table
children.does: Maps three URLs onto handlers. That is the whole of it.
children.built: Direct registration against the app; no router abstraction, no middleware per route.

children.name: Handlers
children.does: Fetches a record by id and 404s when it is missing; lists records with no bound.
children.built: Two async functions calling the store directly and passing results through the serialiser.
children.condition: listRecordsHandler returns a hardcoded empty array and has no pagination design behind it.

children.name: Wire format
children.does: Decides what leaves the building — id, timestamp, account, geo, org. The raw payload never crosses the boundary.
children.built: One pure mapping function from the internal record to the wire shape.

nodes.name: Dashboard
nodes.does: The internal read-only view. Fetches the record list on mount and renders it as a table.
nodes.built: A single React component with one effect and no error state.
nodes.condition: Calls the unbounded list route on every mount, which is how that endpoint gets hammered.

nodes.name: Edge cache
nodes.does: CloudFront in front of the load balancer. Caches GETs for 60 seconds, which is the only reason the list route survives.
nodes.built: A Terraform distribution pointing at the API load balancer, caching GET and HEAD.

nodes.name: Shared schema
nodes.does: The envelope type and the enrichment lookups. Both the write path and the read path stand on this — change it and everything moves.
nodes.built: An interface, a hand-rolled safeParse, and two lookup stubs that currently return 'unknown'.
nodes.condition: The geo and org lookups are stubs; every enriched record in the store carries the placeholder value.

nodes.name: Auth gate
nodes.does: Checks a bearer token against a static allow-list before anything else runs. Nothing gets past it, including ingest.
nodes.built: Middleware installed first in the server factory, reading a comma-separated env var into a Set.
nodes.condition: Static tokens with no rotation and no per-token identity — a leak means changing an env var everywhere at once.

nodes.name: Metrics registry
nodes.does: The only thing that knows whether any of this is working. In-process counters, scraped as text.
nodes.built: A Map of named counters created on first use, rendered into a scrape format on demand.
nodes.condition: Counters are per-process and reset on restart, so a crash loop looks like a quiet system.

nodes.name: Scheduler
nodes.does: Rolls store generations on a clock — current into daily at 03:00, daily into weekly on Sundays.
nodes.built: A static job list wired to a schedule() call, run as its own command from the same image.
nodes.condition: schedule() is an empty stub; no compaction has ever actually run in this repo.

cites.note: job table and the no-op schedule()
scheduler runs as a separate command

nodes.name: Rust gateway
nodes.does: A like-for-like replacement of the ingest gateway in Rust. Finished, tested, and receiving no traffic.
nodes.built: An axum router with one POST route that parses and appends, returning 202 or 422.
nodes.condition: Nothing routes to it. The cutover has no owner and no date.

nodes.name: Rust workers
nodes.does: The shard pool rewritten on tokio tasks. Same shape as the Node workers, one fin per shard.
nodes.built: A JoinSet spawning one task per shard, awaited to completion.
nodes.condition: enrich_shard is an empty body behind the MERIDIAN_RUST feature gate — the port was never finished.

cites.note: JoinSet fan-out and the empty shard body

steps.caption: The bearer token is checked before anything else runs.
Ingest is mounted on the same server, so the POST lands in the gateway.
The envelope is appended to the durable log — [[the caller is not acknowledged until this returns]].
A worker shard picks the segment up on its next tick.
The enriched record is filed into the current generation.
A read walks the generations until it finds the record.
The response is cached for 60 seconds at the edge.
